question.prompt: Which of the following numbers is a perfect square?

solutions.explanation:
The neighboring factorials share almost all their factors. Recall that \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots n\), so \((n+1)!=(n+1)n!\). Each choice has the form \(n!(n+1)!/2\), with \(n=14,15,16,17,18\), respectively.

Since each of these factorials is even, \(n!/2\) is an integer. Rewrite the expression as
\[
\frac{n!(n+1)!}{2}
=\left(\frac{n!}{2}\right)^2 2(n+1).
\]
An integer square has an even exponent on every prime factor. Multiplying by the displayed square adds only even exponents, so we need only examine \(2(n+1)\). For choices A through E, these factors are
\[
30,\quad32,\quad34,\quad36,\quad38.
\]
The numbers \(30,34,38\) each contain exactly one factor of \(2\), and \(32=2^5\), so these four choices cannot be squares. But \(36=6^2\), giving
\[
\frac{17!18!}{2}
=\left(6\cdot\frac{17!}{2}\right)^2
=(3\cdot17!)^2.
\]
Thus the perfect square is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Expose the square factor
